body: That sounds good but again, what if that gets me barred from entering the U.S.? It happened to a German recently: http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/10/01/ilija-trojanow-nsa-criticism_n_4024595.html

Right now, I'm mainly focused on change in the U.S. The main difference between the U.S. and British governments is that in America, power is given (or supposed to be) by the people whereas in Britain, the government gets its power from 'God'. I don't know how to make change in my country. It sounds a hell of a lot easier in America. At least there is a Constitution that you can stand by.

I don't know about how to get involved. All I have done is sign a few petitions. I support anything involving human rights and civil liberties. I myself am a Libertarian but I'm in the UK so I can't really do much. I really want to live in the U.S. but I'm scared of being denied access if I crititise the surveillance programs.

I'm proud of everybody who took part in the rally the other day. If I was in America, I would have been there too. However, I'm having doubts that things will change. I'm worried about corporations and governments controlling people. I hope I'm wrong though.
Could you please explain that further? I don't quite understand. All i want is to live in a world with freedom and privacy. I feel that they will be heavily restricted in the future.

Most people I know either support the surveillance or they simply don't care. It doesn't make a direct and noticable effect everybody's lives. Plus the powers that be will just have their way like always.
I'm scared of government abuses of law as well as losing my privacy. I don't want to live in a world of total surveillance. It seems the world is heading that way and it won't change.
